place/adana: Central district and city in Adana Province, Turkey.
place/aden: A port in southern Yemen on the Indian Ocean, a major station on the maritime trade routes — al-Muqaddasi's 'vestibule of China' .
place/adra: A small coastal town with no wall, having a bath, an inn and plentiful water; a large river to its west, which the author says rises in the Shilir mountain, reaches the sea here.
place/africa: The African continent, to which Islam spread from Egypt and the Maghreb to the Sahel and the east.
place/aghmat: A city in the far Maghreb. The author names its merchants as travellers on the desert road with Sijilmasa and Draa toward the land of Ghana .
place/agra: A city in northern India; it was the Mughal capital in the reign of Akbar and holds the Taj Mahal.
place/aksum: Capital of the Christian kingdom of Aksum in the Ethiopian highlands, where early Muslims took refuge around 615 CE.
place/alanya: District and town in Antalya, Turkey.
place/aleppo: Aleppo is a city in northern Syria on the river Kuwayk, among the oldest inhabited cities in the world, first mentioned in the twentieth century BC.
place/allaf-yemen: A mountain where the Akilis fortify themselves, to which Ahmad ibn Abbad went out after the safe-conduct.
place/amman: A city in al-Balqa', two days from Jerusalem, near the Ghawr.
place/anapa: A former fortress on the Black Sea, on the Bugur river some 40 km south-west of the Kuban estuary, built by French engineers for Sultan Abd al-Hamid I in 1781.
place/arafat: A broad plain outside Mecca where pilgrims stand on the Day of Arafat.
place/arsuf: A small fishing port on the Palestinian coast, about ten miles north of Jaffa; its Arabic name probably preserves its original dedication to the Semitic god Reseph.
place/ashir: A city known as Ashir of Ziri, with a sandy plain and spring water, near Sutayt.
place/aswan: A small, prosperous town with plenty of wheat, vegetables and meat.
place/asyut: A city in Upper Egypt on the west bank of the Nile, about three miles from it, with palm groves around it and an old wall.
place/athens: Capital of Greece. Muslims first came into contact with the town in 283 AH (896), when Saracen pirates occupied it briefly.
place/ayla: A town whose master Ibn Ishaq names as Yuhanna ibn Ru'ba, who made peace with the Prophet at Tabuk and paid him the jizya.
place/badr: Settlement in the Hejaz, southwest of Medina, near the wells where the Battle of Badr was fought in 624 CE.
place/baku: Capital of Azerbaijan on the Caspian's Absheron peninsula; the medieval Shirvanshah walled city, later an oil-boom town of the Russian empire and the Soviet Union.
place/balkh: Balkh, the city of the Tukhara; al-Ahnaf's march won its sulh at four or — the sounder report — seven hundred thousand, Asid ibn al-Mutashammis (or al-Ahnaf's nephew) left over it.
place/basra: Basra is a city of lower Mesopotamia on the Shatt al-Arab, grown from a military camp that Utba ibn Ghazwan set up on the orders of Umar ibn al-Khattab during the early conquests.
place/bastam: A fine town with a wall, standing markets and tax-collection, one stage from Gurgan on the road to Damghan.
place/bayhaq: Bayhaq, a rustaq of Naysabur; the ascetic al-Aswad ibn Kulthum breached its walls and fell with his band before Adham ibn Kathum won the town.
place/bengal: Historical region of the eastern Indian subcontinent, today split between Bangladesh and West Bengal.
place/bhopal: Metropolis and state capital in Madhya Pradesh, India.
place/bitlis: Central district and city in Bitlis Province, Turkey.
place/bolu: Central district and city in Bolu Province, Turkey.
place/bornu: Historic kingdom of the central Sudan around Lake Chad.
place/bosnia: Balkan land largely Islamised under Ottoman rule.
place/brunei: Sovereign country and sultanate on the island of Borneo in south-east Asia, member of the Commonwealth of Nations.
place/buda: Western part of Budapest, Hungary, former independent city.
place/buhran: A place in the Hijaz, in the area of al-Fara', which the text describes as a mine.
place/bursa: Anatolian city on the northern foothills of Mysian Olympus, the ancient Prusa; taken by the Ottomans on 6 April 1326 and their main capital until 1402 .
place/bust: Bust of Sijistan; taken by Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura by compact with Zabil.
place/cairo: Capital of Egypt and one of the most important centres of religious, cultural and political life in the Muslim world, on both banks of the Nile south of the delta.
place/ceuta: A city on the Strait of Gibraltar, from which Ibn Jubayr took ship on his journey to the Hijaz.
place/chios: Greek island in the Aegean Sea.
place/crimea: Eastern European peninsula, in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov, disputed between Ukraine (de jure) and Russia (de facto).
place/dakar: Capital and the largest city of Senegal.
place/delhi: A city in northern India on the west bank of the Yamuna.
place/dhaka: The capital of Bangladesh; it became capital of the Bengal region in the Mughal era in the early seventeenth century CE.
place/dhamar: A city in Yemen forty-eight miles from Sanaa, on the valley road that runs past it.
place/doha: Capital of Qatar on the Gulf; seat of the Al Thani government and the country's political and commercial centre.
place/dubai: City on the Gulf coast, seat of the emirate of Dubai ruled by the Al Maktoum; a pearling port that became the commercial hub of the United Arab Emirates.
place/erbil: Capital of Kurdistan Region in Iraq.
place/france: Country in Western Europe and other continents (through its overseas territories in America, Africa and Oceania).
place/gaza: A city on the Palestinian coast with a harbour, about twenty miles from Ascalon.
place/ghazna: A great, populous city with many markets, from which the road enters the lands of India, which al-Idrisi lists on the Bust road.
place/haifa: A town below the tip of Mount Carmel with a good harbour for fleets, three light stages from Qaysariyya.
place/hama: A Syrian city on the Orontes, famous for its water-wheels; a branch of the Ayyubid family ruled it, and it is the home of the historian Abu al-Fida.
place/harat: Herat, a city of Khurasan; to it Fayruz exiled the Persians whose descendants joined the Turkish Hayatila aiding Quhistan.
place/hawth-yemen: A place where al-Hadi camped with his army in the days past of Safar 286 AH to face al-Da'am at Khiwan; the editor's footnote refers to al-Hamdani's Sifat Jazirat al-Arab, p.
place/hijaz: Historic region of western Arabia containing Mecca, Medina and Jeddah, the cradle of Islam.
place/hilla: A city in Iraq on the Euphrates near Babylon, passed through by Ibn Jubayr on his way to Syria.
place/hulwan: town at the foot of the Mah mountains; in al-Baladhuri Yazdgard fled there from al-Mada'in with his asawira, treasuries, women and children, departing after Jalula.
place/humdan: Humdan — the Chinese great king's capital in Abu Dulaf's account
place/iran: Country in western Asia, heartland of Persianate Islamic civilisation; historic Persia.
place/izmir: A coastal city in western Anatolia on the Aegean Sea.
place/jaen: A fine city rich in fertile land, honey and meat, with running springs beneath its wall and a strong citadel; the author says more than three thousand villages around it raise silkworms.
place/java: The largest island of what is now Indonesia.
place/jazirat-ibn-umar: A town on the Tigris, in northern Iraq and southern Turkey today, which Ibn Battuta mentions under the name Jazirat Ibn Umar.
place/jeddah: Red Sea port of the Hejaz, the main gateway for pilgrims to Mecca since the time of the caliph Uthman.
place/jurjan: The province at the Caspian's corner; its king treated with Sa'id ibn al-As for two hundred thousand dirhams in the 29 AH Tabaristan campaign.
place/kano: A city in northern Nigeria, among the oldest centres of Islam in the Hausa lands.
place/kashan: Iranian city on the desert edge, a centre of learning and Sufism.
place/kazan: City in the Republic of Tatarstan, Russia.
place/khaqan: A large city to the north on a great river with fertile banks, with trade and crafts, and the herds of the district; six stages from Nadkhu.
place/khiwan: A strong fortress with two water pools and vineyards whose large grapes are dried into raisins and carried to neighbouring lands; it lies on the road to Sa'da.
place/khoy: City in West Azarbaijan Province, Iran.
place/kirman: a province; in al-Baladhuri, Yazdgard's refuge where he scorned its marzban, and where the damaq destroyed Mujashi' ibn Mas'ud's army at Bimandh.
place/konya: Anatolian city, capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum from the reign of Mas'ud I (512-550/1118-1155) and the burial place of Rumi (d.
place/kufa: Kufa was one of the two garrison cities founded by early Islam in Iraq, established by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas in 17 AH, 638 CE, on the right bank of the Euphrates near al-Hira.
place/lahore: A major city of the Punjab on the left bank of the Ravi; its earliest surviving mention is in the Hudud al-'alam of 372/982.
place/lisbon: Lisbon (Ushbuna) — the Atlantic city of western al-Andalus, today's capital of Portugal; its district near Santarem held a gold mine .
place/madar-yemen: A place in Yemen to which Ali ibn Sulayman went after being put out of Sana'a and where al-Hadi halted in 288 AH, staying some days until Abdullah ibn al-Husayn came to him.
place/madyan: A large town on the Red Sea coast which al-Idrisi identifies as the town of Shu'ayb, with a house and water from a flowing spring; its livelihood is narrow, five stages from Ayla.
place/makran: Makran, the coastal land between Fars and Sind; stormed and garrisoned by Sinan ibn Salama — Ibn al-Kalbi names Hakim ibn Jabala — and mourned in A'sha Hamdan's famous verses.
place/malay: The town where the king of the Island of the Moon lives, on that long island .
place/mali: Sahel state on the land of the old Mali empire.
place/malta: A large island with a town, its bay opening to the east, described as abundant; a channel's distance from Sicily.
place/mardin: A city in south-eastern Turkey on the Jazira road, which Ibn Battuta mentions on his journey.
place/mecca: The most sacred city of Islam, in the Hejaz about 72 km inland from Jeddah, where the Prophet Muhammad was born, the Kaaba stands and the annual Hajj is held.
place/medina: City in the Hejaz to which the Prophet migrated in 622 CE; site of the Prophet's Mosque and the first Muslim community.
place/meknes: A handsome city on high ground with water running to its east, with markets, baths and houses, and gardens and fields around it; named after the Miknasa tribe.
place/merv: An ancient city in present-day Turkmenistan; it was the capital of Khurasan, the Abbasid movement set out from it, and al-Ma'mun resided there before moving to Baghdad.
place/mihran: Mihran, Sind's great river and its land; here Muhammad ibn al-Qasim camped mid-way, crossed the Mihwan by a contrived bridge, and Dahir fell at evening.
place/mina: A valley between Makkah and al-Mash'ar, where pilgrims throw the jamarat (pebbles) and spend the nights of the Days of Tashriq.
place/minas-najran: A place in the Najran account below whose fort Ibn Bustam drew up Banu al-Harith and the people of Minas against Abu Muhammad in 286 AH.
place/moscow: Capital and most populous city of Russia.
place/mostar: Ottoman city of Herzegovina on the Neretva, famous for its sixteenth-century bridge Stari Most and its madrasas and Muslim quarters; devastated in the 1990s war and rebuilt.
place/mosul: A city on the west bank of the Tigris in northern Mesopotamia, opposite Nineveh, and in early Islamic times the capital of Diyar Rabi'a in the Jazira.
place/multan: A city in southern Punjab in Pakistan, conquered by Muhammad ibn al-Qasim in 712 CE; it is an important centre of Sufism.
place/mumbai: India's largest city and chief Arabian Sea port; formerly Bombay.
place/murcia: A city on the river that bears its name; the author gives its distance from Lorca as forty miles.
place/muscat: The capital of the Sultanate of Oman on the Gulf of Oman, an old trading port; Oman is the centre of the Ibadi school.
place/nablus: The city of the Samaritans, with the well where, as the people of Jerusalem say, a visitor asked a Samaritan woman for water; a day from Ramla.
place/najaf: A city in Iraq containing the shrine of Ali ibn Abi Talib, which Ibn Battuta mentions on his way to Iraq.
place/nasa: Nasa of Khurasan; Ibn Khazim took its Humrandiz rustaq and its lord truced at three hundred thousand — or on land-capacity kharaj, with no killing and no captives.
place/nawa: Nawa: a village of the Hawran south of Damascus in the Jawlan , known in the seventh Islamic century as the birthplace of Imam Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi (d.
place/ohrid: Town and seat of Ohrid Municipality, North Macedonia.
place/oman: The land of Oman, which al-Idrisi describes as self-contained and well peopled, with bananas, pomegranates, figs, grapes and other fruit.
place/paris: Capital and most populous city in France.
place/patna: Metropolis and state capital of Bihar, India.
place/qatar: The Qatari peninsula on the western Gulf; a pearling coast under Al Thani rule, a British protectorate until 1971, and an independent emirate since.
place/qazwin: City in the Daylam mountain country; in al-Baladhuri the asawira living opposite Daylam converted when the Muslims came to Qazwin, on the terms of Basra's asawira.
place/quba: A village at the southern approach of Medina where the Prophet stopped on 8 Rabi' I 1 AH, stayed four days on Ibn Ishaq's account, and founded the first mosque 'upon taqwa'.
place/qumm: a Jibal city; in al-Baladhuri reached by Abu Musa and Abdallah ibn Qays returning from Nihawand — stayed upon days, then opened.
place/rabat: Capital of Morocco on the Bou Regreg estuary; an Almohad ribat town that became the seat of the Alawite sultans.
place/rashid: A civilised town on the Nile with farms, wheat and barley, fine vegetables and fresh fruit, and much Nile fish, including the dulays fish carried to other regions; sixty miles from Alexandria.
place/raydah-yemen: A town a day's journey from Sana'a according to the editor's footnote from Mu'jam al-Buldan, where al-Hadi fought Sa'sa'a ibn Ja'far and razed its palace at the end of Jumada II 288 AH.
place/rayy: An ancient city near present-day Tehran, among the largest cities of the Persian lands in the Abbasid era; the physician Abu Bakr al-Razi is ascribed to it.
place/rhodes: Island city held by the Knights Hospitaller; Mehmed II's siege of 1480 was repelled.
place/riyadh: Capital of Saudi Arabia in Najd; seat of the Saudi state since its first emirate, rebuilt as the modern royal capital after 1932.
place/ruse: City in People's Republic of Bulgaria.
place/safad: The principal town of Upper Galilee on a commanding hill.
place/safwan: A valley in the Badr district; the Prophet reached it in Rabi' al-Awwal of 2 AH, pursuing Kurz ibn Jabir al-Fihri, who had raided Medina's pastures, but did not catch him.
place/sawhan-najran: A place near Najran with a fort where a group of Banu al-Harith gathered and where al-Hadi fought in the fight of that name.
place/sawl: A large village with markets, palms and fruit, at the mouth of the canal called Khalij al-Manha.
place/sfax: A city on the Tunisian coast, which Ibn Battuta mentions on his way to Tripoli.
place/shama: A small town in Zaghawa country, like a large village.
place/sidon: Coastal city in Lebanon south of Beirut.
place/siffin: A plain on the Euphrates in northern Syria where Muawiya camped first and cut the water from Ali's army; Ali camped opposite, and the battle of Siffin took place there in 37 AH .
place/silves: Silves (Shalb) — capital of the Kura of Ossonoba in western al-Andalus, 'a fine seat with towns and strongholds' beside Lisbon's district .
place/sinjar: A town in northern Iraq on the Jazira road, which Ibn Battuta passed through on his way from Nasibin to Mosul.
place/sivas: Central district and city in Sivas Province, Turkey.
place/sokoto: A city in Nigeria, capital of Sokoto State.
place/sousse: A city on the Tunisian coast, which Ibn Battuta passed through on his journey.
place/suways: Two towns that stood at Qulzum, now mostly in ruins; al-Idrisi says their people drank from the Suways spring, a brackish spring hard to drink.
place/syria: Syria; a place linked to persons via Wikidata claims.
place/tabriz: Tabriz is the traditional capital of the Persian province of Azerbaijan, set on an alluvial plain near Lake Urmiya and prone to earthquakes.
place/tabuk: Town in northwest Arabia, the furthest point of the Prophet's expedition of 630 CE toward the Byzantine frontier.
place/tarim: A great city of Hadramawt in al-Hamdani's register of the valley's towns, listed after Shabwa and before Daw'an .
place/tehran: Capital of Iran at the foot of the Alborz; made the Qajar seat in 1788, it is the country's political, scholarly and publishing centre.
place/tihama: A low coastal land between the Red Sea and the mountains of Yemen, running from the Qulzum coast to Aden in about twelve stages, with mountains to the east and the sea to the west.
place/tokat: Central district and city in Tokat Province, Turkey.
place/tulaytula: Toledo, the Gothic capital of al-Andalus on the Tagus; Tariq ibn Ziyad took it and seized there the great table Musa ibn Nusayr presented to al-Walid at Damascus in 96.
place/tunis: Tunis is the capital of modern Tunisia, founded by the Arabs at the end of the seventh century on the site of an older city called Tunes, inland beside a lagoon and distinct from coastal Carthage.
place/tustar: In al-Baladhuri: a town where Jaban massed in a great host; Khalid sent al-Muthanna ibn Haritha and Hanzala the Scribe against him, and he fled at their approach.
place/ukbara: Town on the Tigris; in al-Baladhuri its people were safe-conducted by al-Nusayr and brought food and fodder to his men.
place/urmia: City in West Azerbaijan Province, Iran.
place/varna: City in Varna municipality, Varna oblast, Bulgaria.
place/vienna: Vienna; a place linked to persons via Wikidata claims.
place/wahran: A city on the coast with a well-built earthen wall, set markets and crafts; it faces Almeria on the Andalusian shore across the sea.
place/wasaha-yemen: A town in rough mountains near Harad according to the editor's footnote, which al-Hadi entered in Shawwal 284 AH, staying eight days.
place/yanbu: Red Sea port on the Hejaz coast, long the port of Medina.
place/yazd: A populous city of low prices, about thirty miles east of Kath, on the edge of a desert that joins the Khurasan road.
place/yemen: The southwest corner of Arabia, homeland of the Qahtani Arabs and seat of the successive Sabaean, Himyarite, Abyssinian and Persian powers narrated in the sira's prologue.
place/zabid: Yemeni coastal town, a centre of Islamic learning in the later Middle Ages and a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1993.
place/zanjan: A town in Qazwin's marches; al-Bara' ibn Azib took it by force after Qazwin's treaty and his raids on Daylam, Jilan, al-Babar and al-Taylasan.
